output.name: Tikar — The Small Boot (The Unflown)
output.myth: The mother of a girl called Tikar sewed her seal-hide boots the winter she turned five. On the first warm day one went into the surf off the Kess rocks, and the sea kept it. The other hung by the fire so the household would know it was half a pair. Hesk, who keeps count, found the tally one short and would not let it lie. Ennu the Kite-Wright cut a cuff from the Reel's last strand and flew the boot into the Unflown, where no boat goes. It hangs there a hand-span from the Unlaid Rope, where the dead do not stay knotted. South-west, Skelmi the Unstitched Gull still waits for its last feather, the needle stuck in the wing. North-west, the eleven rowers of Tormesk watch from a boat that will not turn for any prayer. Sil walks the shore at night looking for it too. The old women say that when a gull calls a child's name over the water, you do not answer. The Unflown keeps what is half of something. It is patient, and it is not finished with you yet.
output.finding: From Tormesk, the Count of Oars, Tikar lies one hand-span (about 19°) to the south-east, though islanders never see it from home, and sailors far south find it by going to the Unlaid Rope and looking a hand-span north.
